newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds await U.S. data, spread seen wider.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds await U.S. data, spread seen wider.

text.p: Belgian bonds lost morning gains to close lower with Germany on Thursday, with dealers focussing on U.S. jobs data due 1330 GMT on Friday.
February payrolls are seen at 230,000, from 271,000.
Dealers said they expected trading to be thin and directionless ahead of publication of the figures.
Many also said they were surprised at the further narrowing of the Bund/OLO spread. The 2007 OLO closed with a yield of 5.73%, from 5.70, six bp over Bunds, from eight.
One dealer said that purchases by one large domestic player were part of the reason for the narrowing.
But he added that with the OLO exchange auction coming up on Tuesday, the spread should widen towards the eight to ten bp level again.
Money market yields remained well abouve equivalent German yields in the aftermath of a bribery scandal involving one of the government parties last month.
Three-month T-bills were quoted at 3.35/40 percent, compared to 3.13 percent for equivalent German yields.
